sources.entry: Superagent - Desktop app that gives coding agents like Claude Code and Codex a real browser to drive, an iOS Simulator to install and screenshot apps in, and a phone companion app for remote monitoring.

summary.one_liner: Superagent is an open-source Mac app (Electron, TypeScript, React) that wraps Claude Code, Codex, or Antigravity in a workspace with a live browser, an iOS Simulator pane, and a companion iPhone app for remote monitoring.
summary.what_it_does: Each project is a chat window placed beside a real browser the agent can drive (open pages, click, type, read back) using the user's own logged-in session. An iOS Simulator is streamed into the app at about one frame per second, and the agent can tap, swipe, and type into it. Every chat works in its own git branch copy of the project, which can be kept (folded back as one change) or thrown away. Users can split up to eight chats side by side, pair an iPhone app through end-to-end encrypted relay for remote prompts and yes/no answers, and use a corner tile to ask questions from any app. The README also describes an opt-in computer-use mode for controlling other Mac apps, plus a per-project task board, routines on a timer, and voice dictation transcribed locally. Everything runs on the user's existing agent subscription with no API key or middleman server.
use_cases: watch a coding agent build a web page while seeing the result
let an AI agent test a web app in a browser with my logged-in session
have an agent build and screenshot an iOS app in the simulator
monitor and answer a coding agent from my iPhone
run several parallel coding-agent chats on the same project without conflicts
schedule recurring checks of a website with an agent
notable: Each chat gets its own private git-branch checkout of the project, so parallel agents do not collide
End-to-end encrypted phone pairing through a blind relay that stores nothing; relay can be self-hosted
Agent drives the same visible browser pane the user sees, not a hidden headless browser
Voice dictation is transcribed on the Mac and never leaves it
Opt-in computer use with permission prompts, app allowlists, and an emergency stop shortcut
caveats: Requires a Mac with Apple Silicon; the README lists no other platforms for the desktop app
Requires Claude Code installed and signed in; Xcode is needed only for the simulator and an iPhone only for the companion app
Computer-use and 2.0/2.1 features are in beta and available only through the Beta updates setting; the README warns they may change
